input.productDescription: An independent writer's personal blog that publishes one long-form essay every week or two on cities, technology, and everyday life. The single home page introduces the writer, features the newest essay with an excerpt, lists earlier essays with dates, reading times, and topics, and invites readers to subscribe by email. Readers are people who already follow the writer and read each essay in full, so the reading experience, typography and archive scanning matter more than conversion tricks.
audience: loyal readers who follow one writer and read each essay in full
people interested in cities, urbanism, technology and everyday life
returning subscribers browsing the archive for earlier essays
primaryTasks: read the newest essay's excerpt and continue to the full essay
scan earlier essays by date, reading time and topic
avoid: generic SaaS landing template with hero, three feature cards and logo wall
newsletter-growth dark patterns such as modal popups or countdowns
a headline with one accent-coloured italic word repeated as a formula
constraints: Vite + React + plain CSS only, no UI kits or Tailwind
no external image URLs and no stock photos
single responsive page for phones and desktops
no webfont network dependency unless self-contained

product.productDescription: An independent writer's blog publishing one long-form essay every week or two on cities, technology, and everyday life. One home page: writer intro, newest essay with excerpt, archive of earlier essays with dates, reading times and topics, and an email subscribe invitation. Readers follow the writer and read each essay in full.
primaryTasks: scan earlier essays by date, reading time and topic

Judgement with the page open at 1440 and 375. The opening is a magazine feature opener: title, one-sentence deck, one action, then the essay's own words. Its visual, 'Inside this essay', is this essay's real structure (four parts and minutes) with the filled stop marking where the excerpt comes from; it would be nonsense on another product. No hero tagline + feature trio + testimonial + CTA, no stock or abstract imagery, no italic-accent headline. Editorial Silence is visible: serif display, paper-white surface, hairline rules, 0 radius, no shadow, one restrained ink-blue accent. Copy is concrete (named streets, counts, dates). On phones the same structure runs in one column and nav wraps instead of hiding. Remaining judgement calls: the writer, essays and dates are invented sample content, and essay links point to /essays/<slug> pages this brief does not build.
